title: Tech Trends 2015: The fusion of business and IT
notes: 'Deloitte’s sixth Technology Trends report' (2010 counts as the first). Eight trends (entries 1-8): 'Over the next 18–24 months, each of these trends could potentially disrupt the way businesses engage their customers, how work gets done, and how markets and industries evolve.' Plus an 'Exponentials' chapter on six exponential technologies (entries 9-14), written with Singularity University faculty; it states no time horizon for them. Quotes for trends are from each chapter's opening abstract; for exponentials, from the opening of each section. Read from the Wayback Machine copy of the Deloitte Global PDF. Published month not stated.

entries.label: CIO as chief integration officer
entries.quote: As technology transforms existing business models and gives rise to new ones, the role of the CIO is evolving rapidly, with integration at the core of its mission.
entries.subject: CIO role
entries.note: Chapter subtitle: 'A new charter for IT'.

entries.label: API economy
entries.quote: Application programming interfaces (APIs) have been elevated from a development technique to a business model driver and boardroom consideration.
entries.subject: APIs and the API economy
entries.note: Chapter subtitle: 'From systems to business services'.

entries.label: Ambient computing
entries.quote: Ambient computing is the backdrop of sensors, devices, intelligence, and agents that can put the Internet of Things to work.
entries.subject: Internet of Things (ambient computing)
entries.note: Chapter subtitle: 'Putting the Internet of Things to work'.

entries.label: Dimensional marketing
entries.quote: A new vision for marketing is being formed as CMOs and CIOs invest in technology for marketing automation, next-generation omnichannel approaches, content development, customer analytics, and commerce initiatives.
entries.subject: Digital marketing technology
entries.note: Chapter subtitle: 'New rules for the digital age'.

entries.label: Software-defined everything
entries.quote: The entire operating environment—server, storage, and network—can now be virtualized and automated.
entries.subject: Software-defined infrastructure

entries.label: Core renaissance
entries.quote: To this end, many organizations are modernizing systems to pay down technical debt, replatforming solutions to remove barriers to scale and performance, and extending their legacy infrastructures to fuel innovative new services and offerings.
entries.subject: Core system modernization
entries.note: Chapter subtitle: 'Revitalizing the heart of IT'.

entries.label: Amplified intelligence
entries.quote: Artificial intelligence is now a reality. Its more promising application, however, is not replacing workers but augmenting their capabilities.
entries.subject: Augmented intelligence (AI and advanced analytics)

entries.label: IT worker of the future
entries.quote: To tackle these challenges, companies will likely need to cultivate a new species—the IT worker of the future—with habits, incentives, and skills that are inherently different from those in play today.
entries.subject: Technology talent and workforce

entries.label: Artificial intelligence
entries.quote: Although artificial intelligence (AI) may still conjure up futuristic visions of cyborgs and androids, it is becoming embedded in everyday life, and supporting significant strides in everything from medical systems to transportation.
entries.subject: Artificial intelligence

entries.label: Robotics
entries.quote: AI and exponential improvements in technology are bringing what were once futuristic visions into the mainstream of business and society.
entries.subject: Robotics

entries.label: Additive manufacturing
entries.quote: Centuries later, the technology, commonly referred to as 3D printing, holds the potential of eliminating some long-standing trade-offs between cheap and good by potentially erasing the cost of complexity.
entries.subject: Additive manufacturing (3D printing)

entries.label: Quantum computing
entries.quote: The potential power of quantum computing stems from its ability to free computing from sequential binary operations.
entries.subject: Quantum computing

entries.label: Industrial biology
entries.quote: Today, however, digital technologies are fueling the field of industrial and digital biology, ushering in a renaissance in the ability to manipulate DNA, splice genes, and control genomes.
entries.subject: Industrial and synthetic biology

entries.label: Cyber security
entries.quote: Cybercrime has traditionally been a two-dimensional problem: individuals hiding behind computer screens and hacking into the world’s information systems. That’s about to change as cybercrime goes 3D.
entries.subject: Cybersecurity (physical-cyber threats)
